text:
aline: Heads-up — onboarding run for model `hera-7b` is failing schema checks in CI; attaching snippet. CI error says missing defaults for `quantization` and `max_batch_tokens`, and tokenizer eos id mismatch with runtime. anyone seen this pattern before?

sam: I saw similar with the katana import last quarter. Quick wins: add explicit defaults in config.json and bump `schema_version`. Can you paste the failing config?

aline: here's the file we pushed: 
```json
{
  \"model_name\": \"hera-7b\",
  \"weights\": \"s3://redwood-models/hera-7b/v1/pytorch_model.bin\",
  \"schema_version\": \"2.0\",
  \"tokenizer\": {\"path\": \"s3://redwood-models/hera-7b/tokenizer.json\"}
}
```
CI log: `SchemaError: missing required field 'quantization' (at /)` and `TokenizerMismatch: tokenizer.eos_token_id=2 but runtime expects 1`

ci-bot: build 4732 failed — schema-validator v1.4.0 returned exit code 2. See http://ci.internal/4732 for logs.

jia: Two things: 1) The schema_validator enforces new defaults starting schema_version 2.1 (we shipped the stricter rules for Dedicated last month). 2) We intentionally stopped assuming eos_token_id=1 because some HF tokenizers use 2. For serving we support a `tokenizer_overrides` block in config.json to map expectations.

maya: For this model the tokenizer.json from the vendor sets eos_token_id=2. Canary lab runtime still uses 1 as internal sentinel. Options: change runtime assumption (risky mid-release) or set \"tokenizer_overrides\" in model config to normalize to 1. Example: 
```json
\"tokenizer_overrides\": { \"eos_token_id\": 1 }
```
That worked for the katana import.

sam: Also add `quantization` default: 
```json
\"quantization\": { \"type\": \"none\", \"bits\": 16 }
```
and `max_batch_tokens\": 2048` (or use autosuggest from optimize). We should update schema docs too.

validator-bot: Suggested autofix diff available at https://git.internal/redwood/validators/patches/patch-981. Patch summary: set schema_version->2.1, add quantization default, add tokenizer_overrides mapping.

tom: quick question — will bumping schema_version to 2.1 break older Dedicated clusters? We have a migration path but need to ensure Dedicated control plane accepts 2.1 configs until clusters are upgraded.

jia: Good call. The validator will accept 2.0 and 2.1 but will flag missing fields only for 2.1. If we set schema_version: 2.0 in the model config CI will skip stricter checks — but we prefer 2.1 so the model behaves correctly in hosted. Two approaches: (A) keep 2.0 for now and open a ticket to migrate Dedicated clusters, or (B) include all defaults in the config and set 2.1 so it's forward-compatible. I recommend B.

aline: I'm leaning B too. I'll open a small PR with the autofix changes and include a migration note. PR will be <#PR-6521>. pinging @sam @jia for review, @maya for tokenizer sanity check.

sam: :thumbsup: please include a one-liner in the changelog explaining why `tokenizer_overrides` is necessary (runtime sentinel mismatch).

maya: :eyes: I'll look after lunch. If ci-bot still fails after patch, we might need a quick runtime patch to log the tokenizer mapping at load time for easier debugging.

aline: PR opened 6521 — linking patch. Running local validator before pushing. Thanks all.

validator-bot: Note: after PR apply, run `make validate-schema` locally or CI will auto-queue a backfill job.

ci-bot: build queued 4733 (after PR push).

tom: minor nit — please use full S3 URIs with region tag in weights (we had a 502 once due to missing region). e.g. `s3://eu-west-1/redwood-models/...`

aline: good catch — will update weights path too.

sam: LGTM for the plan. If anyone wants to pair on the patch I can help review tonight.

aline: thanks — closing thread once CI green. :white_check_mark:
